slides.say: Five different letters are put into three mailboxes. A mailbox may get any number of letters, or none. In how many different ways can the letters be put into the mailboxes?
So every letter goes into some mailbox. And one mailbox may get several letters.
We'll solve it in two different ways. Let's start with the math way. Like in the lesson, we ask who chooses. Each letter must go somewhere, so each letter chooses a mailbox.
Letter one has three options. Letter two also has three, because a mailbox can take more than one letter. And so on, five letters with three options each.
at: five letters with three options each

slides.say: Three times three times three times three times three. Three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one, two hundred forty-three.
That's three to the power of five.
at: That's three to the power of five

slides.say: The trap is five to the power of three, a hundred twenty-five, choice number one. That lets each mailbox choose one letter. But a mailbox can get two letters, or none.
at: five to the power of three

slides.say: [pause] Not sure which number is the base? Let's plug in small numbers, two letters and two boxes, and list.
Both letters in box one, or both in box two. Or one in each box, in two ways. Four ways.
Four is two squared. That's the number of boxes, to the power of the number of letters.
So here it's three to the power of five again.
at: three to the power of five again

slides.say: Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
